abel-beth-maacah_5.name: Abel-beth-maacah
abel-beth-maacah_5.what: A fortified town in the far north of Israel, near Dan, repeatedly struck by invading armies.
abel-beth-maacah_5.today: Tel Abel Beth Maacah, near Metula, northern Israel.
key: Joab besieged the rebel Sheba in Abel of Beth-maacah until a wise woman had his head thrown out (2 Samuel 20).
Ben-hadad of Syria attacked Israelite cities including Ijon, Dan, and Abel-beth-maacah (1 Kings 15).
Tiglath-pileser of Assyria captured Abel-beth-maacah and carried its people into exile (2 Kings 15).

abel-shittim_10.name: Abel-shittim
abel-shittim_10.what: Israel's final camp on the plains of Moab, east of the Jordan opposite Jericho.
abel-shittim_10.today: Possibly Tell el-Hammam, east of the Jordan opposite Jericho, Jordan.
key: While camped at Shittim, Israel worshiped Baal of Peor with Moabite women, and a plague followed (Numbers 25).
Israel camped along the Jordan from Beth-jeshimoth to Abel-shittim in the plains of Moab (Numbers 33).
Joshua secretly sent two spies from Shittim to scout Jericho (Joshua 2).

abiezer_11.name: Abiezer
abiezer_11.what: Abiezer is a clan of the tribe of Manasseh, Gideon's family line, not a place.

acco_15.name: Acco
acco_15.what: A Mediterranean port city north of Mount Carmel, in the territory assigned to Asher.
acco_15.today: Acre (Akko), on the coast of northern Israel.
key: Asher failed to drive out the inhabitants of Acco and Sidon (Judges 1).
Sailing from Tyre, Paul landed at Ptolemais and stayed a day with the believers there (Acts 21).

adam_21.name: Adam
adam_21.what: A town in the Jordan Valley upstream from Jericho, where the Jordan's waters stopped for Israel's crossing.
adam_21.today: Likely Tell ed-Damiyeh, near the Damiya Bridge over the Jordan, Jordan.
key: The Jordan's flood waters stood in a heap far upstream at Adam, the city beside Zarethan (Joshua 3).
With the waters cut off, Israel crossed on dry ground opposite Jericho (Joshua 3).

ararat_86.name: Ararat
ararat_86.what: A mountainous land north of Assyria where Noah's ark came to rest after the flood.
ararat_86.today: Eastern Turkey and Armenia, the region of the ancient kingdom of Urartu.
key: As the flood waters receded, the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat (Genesis 8).
After killing their father Sennacherib, his sons escaped to the land of Ararat (2 Kings 19).
Jeremiah summoned the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz against Babylon (Jeremiah 51).

armageddon_91.name: Armageddon
armageddon_91.what: The place where, in John's vision, the kings of the earth assemble for battle on the great day of God.
armageddon_91.today: Commonly linked with Megiddo and the Jezreel Valley, northern Israel.
key: The sixth bowl dries up the Euphrates to prepare the way for the kings from the east (Revelation 16).
Demonic spirits gather the kings of the whole world for battle on the great day of God (Revelation 16).
The kings are assembled at the place called in Hebrew Armageddon (Revelation 16).

baalah_134.name: Baalah
baalah_134.what: A town in Judah's far south toward Edom, later counted among Simeon's towns; not the Baalah that is Kiriath-jearim.
baalah_134.today: Exact site unknown; in the Negeb near Beersheba, southern Israel.
key: Baalah is listed among Judah's southernmost towns in the Negeb toward Edom (Joshua 15).
Balah, likely the same town, was included in Simeon's inheritance within Judah (Joshua 19).
Simeon's descendants lived in Bilhah and nearby towns until David's reign (1 Chronicles 4).

babel_150.name: Babel
babel_150.what: An ancient city in the land of Shinar where people built a tower and God confused their language.
babel_150.today: The ruins of Babylon, near Hillah, Iraq.
key: Nimrod's kingdom began with Babel and other cities in the land of Shinar (Genesis 10).
People settled in Shinar and began building a city and a tower to make a name for themselves (Genesis 11).
The Lord confused their language and scattered them over the face of all the earth (Genesis 11).

beer_164.name: Beer
beer_164.what: A stopping place in Moab where God gave Israel water from a well during the wilderness journey.
beer_164.today: Exact site unknown; north of the Arnon River in Jordan.
key: The Lord told Moses to gather the people at Beer so he could give them water (Numbers 21).
Israel sang a song to the well that the princes and nobles had dug (Numbers 21).

bela_172.name: Bela
bela_172.what: The earlier name of Zoar, a small city near the southern end of the Dead Sea.
bela_172.today: Likely near Safi, southeast of the Dead Sea in Jordan.
key: The king of Bela, that is, Zoar, joined Sodom's alliance against Chedorlaomer and his allies (Genesis 14).
The five kings were defeated in the Valley of Siddim, and Lot was taken captive (Genesis 14).
Lot fled to Zoar, which God spared when fire fell on Sodom (Genesis 19).

berea_177.name: Berea
berea_177.what: A city in Macedonia where the Jews eagerly examined the Scriptures after hearing Paul preach.
key: After the riot in Thessalonica, believers sent Paul and Silas away by night to Berea (Acts 17).
The Bereans examined the Scriptures daily to check Paul's teaching, and many believed (Acts 17).
Jews from Thessalonica stirred up the crowds, so Paul left while Silas and Timothy remained (Acts 17).
Sopater of Berea traveled with Paul toward Jerusalem (Acts 20).

beth-maacah_221.name: Beth-maacah
beth-maacah_221.what: The district of a far-northern town, Abel of Beth-maacah, where the rebel Sheba took refuge from Joab.
beth-maacah_221.today: Tel Abel Beth Maacah, near Metula, northern Israel.
key: Sheba son of Bichri passed through all the tribes and reached Abel of Beth-maacah (2 Samuel 20).
Joab besieged the city and built a siege mound against its wall (2 Samuel 20).
A wise woman persuaded the city to throw Sheba's head to Joab, and the siege ended (2 Samuel 20).

bethel_203.name: Bethel
bethel_203.what: A Canaanite royal city north of Jerusalem, near Ai, conquered by Joshua.
bethel_203.today: Likely Beitin, north of Jerusalem, West Bank.
key: Abram built an altar on a hill between Bethel and Ai (Genesis 12).
Jacob dreamed of a stairway to heaven and named the place Bethel (Genesis 28).
Joshua set an ambush between Bethel and Ai, and the men of Bethel joined the chase (Joshua 8).
The king of Bethel is listed among the kings Joshua defeated (Joshua 12).
Jeroboam set up a golden calf at Bethel for the northern tribes (1 Kings 12).

bethesda_205.name: Bethesda
bethesda_205.what: A pool in Jerusalem near the Sheep Gate, surrounded by covered colonnades where the sick lay.
bethesda_205.today: The Pools of Bethesda, near St. Anne's Church in the Old City of Jerusalem.
key: The pool by the Sheep Gate had five roofed colonnades filled with sick and disabled people (John 5).
Jesus healed a man who had been disabled for thirty-eight years and told him to walk (John 5).
Because the healing happened on the Sabbath, Jewish leaders began to persecute Jesus (John 5).

bochim_252.name: Bochim
bochim_252.what: The place where Israel wept after the angel of the Lord rebuked them for disobedience.
bochim_252.today: Exact site unknown; possibly near Bethel, West Bank.
key: The angel of the Lord came from Gilgal to Bochim and rebuked Israel for making covenants with Canaanites (Judges 2).
The people wept aloud, named the place Bochim, and offered sacrifices to the Lord (Judges 2).

caesarea_philippi_267.name: Caesarea Philippi
caesarea_philippi_267.what: A Roman city at the foot of Mount Hermon, near the sources of the Jordan River.
caesarea_philippi_267.today: Banias, at the foot of Mount Hermon in the Golan Heights.
key: Near Caesarea Philippi, Jesus asked who people said he was, and Peter confessed him as the Christ (Matthew 16).
From then on Jesus began to show that he must suffer, be killed, and be raised (Matthew 16).
Mark records Peter's confession on the way to the villages of Caesarea Philippi (Mark 8).

calno_270.name: Calno
calno_270.what: A city in northern Syria conquered by Assyria, cited as a warning to Israel and Judah.
calno_270.today: Likely Kullani (Tell Tayinat), near Antakya in southern Turkey.
key: Amos told Israel's complacent leaders to look at the fate of Calneh and Hamath (Amos 6).
Isaiah quoted Assyria boasting that Calno had fallen just like Carchemish (Isaiah 10).

casiphia_279.name: Casiphia
casiphia_279.what: A place in Babylonia where a community of Levites and temple servants lived during the exile.
casiphia_279.today: Exact site unknown; in Babylonia, likely near Babylon, Iraq.
key: Finding no Levites among the returnees, Ezra sent men to Iddo, the leader at Casiphia (Ezra 8).
Iddo's community sent Sherebiah and other Levites, along with 220 temple servants, to join Ezra (Ezra 8).

cherith_286.name: Cherith
cherith_286.what: A brook east of the Jordan where God fed Elijah through ravens during the drought.
cherith_286.today: Exact site unknown; a wadi east of the Jordan, possibly Wadi el-Yabis, Jordan.
key: God told Elijah to hide by the brook Cherith, east of the Jordan (1 Kings 17).
Ravens brought Elijah bread and meat morning and evening, and he drank from the brook (1 Kings 17).
When the brook dried up, God sent Elijah to a widow in Zarephath (1 Kings 17).

chezib_291.name: Chezib
chezib_291.what: A town in the lowlands of Judah where Judah's son Shelah was born.
chezib_291.today: Exact site unknown; in the Shephelah of Judah, Israel.
key: Judah's Canaanite wife bore his son Shelah while Judah was at Chezib (Genesis 38).
Achzib, likely the same town, was listed among Judah's lowland towns (Joshua 15).
Micah warned that the houses of Achzib would prove deceptive to Israel's kings (Micah 1).

chorazin_299.name: Chorazin
chorazin_299.what: A Galilean town near Capernaum that saw Jesus' mighty works but did not repent.
chorazin_299.today: Korazim (Khirbet Karazeh), north of the Sea of Galilee, Israel.
key: Jesus pronounced woe on Chorazin and Bethsaida for not repenting despite his mighty works (Matthew 11).
He said Tyre and Sidon would have repented long ago had they seen such works (Matthew 11).
Jesus repeated the warning to Chorazin when sending out the seventy-two (Luke 10).

debir_326.name: Debir
debir_326.what: A landmark on Judah's northern boundary near the Valley of Achor; not the Debir captured by Othniel.
debir_326.today: Exact site unknown; likely between Jerusalem and Jericho, West Bank.
key: Judah's northern boundary went up to Debir from the Valley of Achor (Joshua 15).
From there the border turned north toward Gilgal, opposite the ascent of Adummim (Joshua 15).

dothan_342.name: Dothan
dothan_342.what: A town in the hill country north of Samaria, beside a route used by traveling caravans.
dothan_342.today: Tell Dothan, south of Jenin, West Bank.
key: Joseph found his brothers pasturing flocks at Dothan, where they threw him into a pit (Genesis 37).
The brothers sold Joseph to Ishmaelite traders passing by on their way to Egypt (Genesis 37).
At Dothan, God opened Elisha's servant's eyes to see horses and chariots of fire (2 Kings 6).
God struck the Syrian army with blindness, and Elisha led them to Samaria (2 Kings 6).

dumah_345.name: Dumah
dumah_345.what: An oasis region in northern Arabia, the subject of a brief oracle in Isaiah.
dumah_345.today: Likely Dumat al-Jandal (al-Jawf), northern Saudi Arabia.
key: Dumah is named as a son of Ishmael, whose descendants likely gave the oasis its name (Genesis 25).
In an oracle concerning Dumah, someone calls from Seir asking the watchman about the night (Isaiah 21).
The watchman answers that morning comes, and also the night (Isaiah 21).

dura_347.name: Dura
dura_347.what: A plain in the province of Babylon where Nebuchadnezzar set up his golden image.
dura_347.today: Exact site unknown; near Babylon, Iraq.
key: Nebuchadnezzar set up a golden image ninety feet high on the plain of Dura (Daniel 3).
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego refused to bow and were thrown into the furnace, but God delivered them (Daniel 3).

ecbatana_353.name: Ecbatana
ecbatana_353.what: The capital of Media and a summer residence of Persian kings, where royal records were kept.
key: Darius searched the royal archives, and Cyrus's decree to rebuild the temple was found at Ecbatana (Ezra 6).
Darius then ordered the rebuilding to continue, with costs paid from the royal revenue (Ezra 6).

eden_354.name: Eden
eden_354.what: The region where God planted a garden and placed the first man and woman.
eden_354.today: Exact location unknown; Genesis links it with the Tigris and Euphrates rivers.
key: God planted a garden in Eden and put the man there to work it and keep it (Genesis 2).
After they sinned, God sent Adam and Eve out of Eden and placed cherubim to guard the way (Genesis 3).
God promised to make Zion's wilderness like Eden (Isaiah 51).
Ezekiel described the king of Tyre as having been in Eden, the garden of God (Ezekiel 28).
Joel pictured the land as Eden before the invading army and a desolate wilderness behind it (Joel 2).

emmaus_382.name: Emmaus
emmaus_382.what: A village about seven miles from Jerusalem where the risen Jesus was recognized by two disciples.
emmaus_382.today: Exact site unknown; several villages west of Jerusalem have been proposed.
key: The risen Jesus joined two disciples walking to Emmaus, but they did not recognize him (Luke 24).
He explained how all the Scriptures spoke of the Christ's suffering and glory (Luke 24).
They recognized Jesus when he broke bread, and he vanished from their sight (Luke 24).
The two hurried back to Jerusalem to tell the eleven that the Lord had risen (Luke 24).

gath-rimmon_445.name: Gath-rimmon
gath-rimmon_445.what: A Levitical town listed from the western half-tribe of Manasseh, distinct from Dan's Gath-rimmon.
gath-rimmon_445.today: Exact site unknown; possibly Ibleam, near Jenin, West Bank.
key: Gath-rimmon, with Taanach, was given from the half-tribe of Manasseh to the Kohathite Levites (Joshua 21).
The parallel list of Levitical towns names Aner and Bileam from Manasseh instead (1 Chronicles 6).

geba_448.name: Geba
geba_448.what: The starting point of David's rout of the Philistines; Chronicles names Gibeon in the same account.
geba_448.today: Possibly Gibeon (el-Jib), northwest of Jerusalem, West Bank.
key: When the Philistines came up to the Valley of Rephaim again, God told David to circle behind them (2 Samuel 5).
David struck down the Philistines from Geba to Gezer (2 Samuel 5).
Chronicles records the same victory as from Gibeon to Gezer (1 Chronicles 14).

gethsemane_462.name: Gethsemane
gethsemane_462.what: A garden or olive grove on the Mount of Olives where Jesus prayed and was arrested.
gethsemane_462.today: At the foot of the Mount of Olives, across the Kidron Valley from Jerusalem's Old City.
key: Jesus prayed in anguish at Gethsemane, submitting to his Father's will (Matthew 26).
Judas arrived with an armed crowd, identified Jesus with a kiss, and Jesus was arrested (Matthew 26).
Jesus found Peter, James, and John sleeping three times while he prayed (Mark 14).
John notes the garden lay across the Kidron, where Jesus often met with his disciples (John 18).

gihon_472.name: Gihon
gihon_472.what: One of the four rivers flowing out of Eden, said to wind through the land of Cush.
gihon_472.today: Exact location unknown; one of the rivers of Eden.
key: A river flowed out of Eden to water the garden and divided into four rivers (Genesis 2).
The second river, the Gihon, flows around the whole land of Cush (Genesis 2).

giloh_479.name: Giloh
giloh_479.what: A town in the hill country of Judah, home of David's counselor Ahithophel.
giloh_479.today: Exact site unknown; in the hill country of Judah, possibly near Hebron, West Bank.
key: Giloh is listed among the towns in the hill country of Judah (Joshua 15).
Absalom sent for Ahithophel from his city Giloh to join the conspiracy against David (2 Samuel 15).
When his advice was rejected, Ahithophel went home to his city and hanged himself (2 Samuel 17).

gog_484.name: Gog
gog_484.what: Gog is a ruler in Ezekiel and, with Magog, a name for hostile nations in Revelation, not a place.

gomer_488.name: Gomer
gomer_488.what: A distant northern people and land descended from Japheth, named among Gog's allies.
gomer_488.today: Likely central Turkey, home of the ancient Cimmerians.
key: Gomer is listed as the first son of Japheth, ancestor of a northern people (Genesis 10).
Gomer and all its hordes are named among Gog's allies from the far north (Ezekiel 38).

gur_497.name: Gur
gur_497.what: An ascent near Ibleam in the northern hill country, where Jehu's men wounded King Ahaziah.
gur_497.today: Exact site unknown; near Ibleam, south of Jenin, West Bank.
key: Jehu's men shot King Ahaziah of Judah at the ascent of Gur, near Ibleam (2 Kings 9).
Ahaziah fled to Megiddo and died there, and his servants carried him to Jerusalem (2 Kings 9).

hadrach_504.name: Hadrach
hadrach_504.what: A region in Syria named first in Zechariah's oracle of judgment on Israel's northern neighbors.
hadrach_504.today: Likely the region of Hatarikka, near Hama, Syria.
key: The word of the Lord is against the land of Hadrach, and Damascus is its resting place (Zechariah 9).
The oracle continues with judgment on Hamath, Tyre, Sidon, and the Philistine cities (Zechariah 9).
Zion's king then comes, humble and riding on a donkey (Zechariah 9).

havilah_534.name: Havilah
havilah_534.what: A desert region at the eastern edge of the Ishmaelite and Amalekite lands, toward Arabia.
havilah_534.today: Exact location unknown; likely in northwestern Arabia.
key: Ishmael's descendants settled from Havilah to Shur, east of Egypt (Genesis 25).
Saul defeated the Amalekites from Havilah as far as Shur (1 Samuel 15).

hazazon-tamar_542.name: Hazazon-tamar
hazazon-tamar_542.what: An oasis on the western shore of the Dead Sea, identified in Chronicles with En-gedi.
hazazon-tamar_542.today: En-gedi, on the western shore of the Dead Sea, Israel.
key: Chedorlaomer and his allies defeated the Amorites living in Hazazon-tamar (Genesis 14).
A Moabite and Ammonite army gathered at Hazazon-tamar, that is, En-gedi, against Jehoshaphat (2 Chronicles 20).
After Jehoshaphat sought the Lord, the invading armies turned and destroyed one another (2 Chronicles 20).

hazor_549.name: Hazor
hazor_549.what: A group of Arabian desert settlements, named with Kedar in Jeremiah's oracles; not the Canaanite city.
hazor_549.today: Exact site unknown; in the Arabian desert east of Israel.
key: Jeremiah announced that Nebuchadnezzar would strike Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor (Jeremiah 49).
The people of Hazor were told to flee far away and hide (Jeremiah 49).
Hazor would become a haunt of jackals, desolate forever (Jeremiah 49).

helam_552.name: Helam
helam_552.what: A place east of the Jordan where David defeated the Syrian army allied with Ammon.
helam_552.today: Exact site unknown; east of the Jordan, possibly Alma in southern Syria.
key: Hadadezer's Syrian forces gathered at Helam under his commander Shobach (2 Samuel 10).
David crossed the Jordan, defeated the Syrians at Helam, and Shobach died there (2 Samuel 10).

hierapolis_569.name: Hierapolis
hierapolis_569.what: A city in the Lycus Valley of Asia Minor, near Laodicea and Colossae.
key: Epaphras of Colossae worked hard in prayer for the believers in Laodicea and Hierapolis (Colossians 4).
Paul names Hierapolis with Laodicea and Colossae, neighboring cities where believers gathered (Colossians 4).

holy_place_574.name: Holy Place
holy_place_574.what: The outer room of the tabernacle, in front of the veil that screened off the Most Holy Place.
holy_place_574.today: The tabernacle was a portable tent; it no longer exists.
key: The veil divided the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place, with the table and lampstand outside it (Exodus 26).
Golden bells on Aaron's robe sounded whenever he entered the Holy Place before the Lord (Exodus 28).
The incense altar stood before the veil, and Aaron burned incense there every morning (Exodus 30).
Moses placed the table, lampstand, and golden altar in the tent before the veil (Exodus 40).

hor-haggidgad_579.name: Hor-haggidgad
hor-haggidgad_579.what: One of Israel's campsites during the wilderness wanderings, between Bene-jaakan and Jotbathah.
hor-haggidgad_579.today: Exact site unknown; in the wilderness south of the Dead Sea, possibly in the Arabah.
key: Israel set out from Bene-jaakan and camped at Hor-haggidgad (Numbers 33).
From Hor-haggidgad they moved on and camped at Jotbathah (Numbers 33).
Moses recalled the journey from Moserah to Gudgodah and on to Jotbathah (Deuteronomy 10).

immer_596.name: Immer
immer_596.what: A settlement in Babylonia from which some exiles returned who could not prove their Israelite descent.
immer_596.today: Exact site unknown; in Babylonia, Iraq.
key: Returnees from Immer and nearby places could not prove their families belonged to Israel (Ezra 2).
Nehemiah's copy of the list records the same returnees from Immer (Nehemiah 7).

india_597.name: India
india_597.what: The eastern edge of the Persian Empire, along the Indus River valley.
india_597.today: The Indus Valley region, in modern Pakistan and northwestern India.
key: King Ahasuerus ruled 127 provinces from India to Cush (Esther 1).
Mordecai's decree allowing the Jews to defend themselves went to every province from India to Cush (Esther 8).

javan_627.name: Javan
javan_627.what: The Hebrew name for the Greek peoples, especially the Ionians of western Asia Minor and the Aegean.
javan_627.today: Greece and the western coast of Turkey.
key: Javan is listed as a son of Japheth, ancestor of the coastland peoples (Genesis 10).
Javan is named among distant nations who will hear of the Lord's glory (Isaiah 66).
Javan traded slaves and bronze vessels with the city of Tyre (Ezekiel 27).
In Daniel's vision, the shaggy goat represents the king of Greece (Daniel 8).

jebusite_630.name: Jebusite
jebusite_630.what: The ridge of the Jebusite city, Jerusalem, used as a landmark on Judah's northern boundary.
jebusite_630.today: The City of David, south of the Old City of Jerusalem.
key: Judah's boundary ran up the Valley of Hinnom along the southern slope of the Jebusite city (Joshua 15).
The people of Judah could not drive out the Jebusites living in Jerusalem (Joshua 15).
Benjamin's border went down the Valley of Hinnom, south of the Jebusite slope (Joshua 18).
David captured the stronghold of Zion from the Jebusites (2 Samuel 5).

judah_1280.name: Judah
judah_1280.what: The territory of the tribe of Judah, including its hill country, wilderness, and Negeb south of Jerusalem.
judah_1280.today: The southern West Bank and southern Israel, around Bethlehem and Hebron.
key: Joshua wiped out the Anakim from the hill country of Judah (Joshua 11).
Judah's boundaries and towns were set out by lot (Joshua 15).
Men of Judah bound Samson and handed him over to the Philistines (Judges 15).
The prophet Gad told David to leave his stronghold and go into the land of Judah (1 Samuel 22).
David wrote a psalm of longing for God while in the wilderness of Judah (Psalm 63).

judgment_511.name: Hall of Judgment
judgment_511.what: A cedar-paneled hall in Solomon's palace complex where the king sat to give judgment.
judgment_511.today: Part of Solomon's palace in Jerusalem; it no longer exists.
key: Solomon made the Hall of the Throne, the Hall of Judgment, paneled with cedar from floor to rafters (1 Kings 7).
Solomon built a house for Pharaoh's daughter like this hall (1 Kings 7).

kanah_666.name: Kanah
kanah_666.what: A brook flowing west to the Mediterranean that formed part of the border between Ephraim and Manasseh.
kanah_666.today: Likely Wadi Qanah, which flows west into the Yarkon River, Israel and West Bank.
key: Ephraim's border went west from Tappuah to the brook Kanah and ended at the sea (Joshua 16).
Manasseh's boundary went down to the brook Kanah, though some towns south of it belonged to Ephraim (Joshua 17).

karkor_669.name: Karkor
karkor_669.what: A place in the desert east of the Jordan where Gideon routed the Midianite army.
karkor_669.today: Exact site unknown; east of the Jordan, possibly in Wadi Sirhan, Jordan.
key: Zebah and Zalmunna were at Karkor with about fifteen thousand men, all that remained of their army (Judges 8).
Gideon attacked the unsuspecting camp by the caravan route, routed it, and captured both kings (Judges 8).

leshem_727.name: Leshem
leshem_727.what: A city in the far north captured by the tribe of Dan and renamed Dan.
key: When their territory proved too small, the Danites captured Leshem and renamed it Dan (Joshua 19).
Judges tells the fuller story, calling the city Laish and describing its capture and renaming (Judges 18).

libya_730.name: Libya
libya_730.what: The North African region west of Egypt, including the area around Cyrene.
key: Ezekiel listed Libya among Egypt's allies who would fall by the sword (Ezekiel 30).
Visitors from the parts of Libya near Cyrene heard the gospel in their own language at Pentecost (Acts 2).

luz_738.name: Luz
luz_738.what: A city built in the land of the Hittites by a man spared when Joseph's tribes captured Bethel.
luz_738.today: Exact site unknown; in the land of the Hittites, north of Israel.
key: A man of Luz showed Joseph's spies the way into the city, and he and his family were spared (Judges 1).
He went to the land of the Hittites, built a city, and named it Luz (Judges 1).
